name: The delta rule for linear transformers (DeltaNet origin)
aka: Delta Net; delta-rule fast weight programmer; DPFP feature map

source.title: Linear Transformers Are Secretly Fast Weight Programmers

secondary.label: The delta rule itself: Widrow & Hoff, ADALINE / LMS (1960) — historical, not fetched
Parallelised over sequence length (Yang et al.)
RWKV-7 'Goose' — generalised delta rule with vector-valued gating (Mar 2025)

firstShipped.model: Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B (as Gated DeltaNet, 3:1 with gated attention) — first frontier-lab production model; RWKV-7 'Goose' (Mar 2025, 0.1–2.9B open weights) shipped a generalised delta-rule update earlier

problem: Linear attention (2020) has the right bill — O(1) state, O(n) time — but its memory is a sum: S += v·kᵀ. It cannot *overwrite* an old value for a key, so retrieval degrades once you store more associations than the state can hold, and elu+1 / random features were weak kernels anyway.
idea: Treat the linear-attention state as fast weights and update it with the 1960 delta rule: S_t = S_{t−1} + β_t (v_t − S_{t−1}φ(k_t)) φ(k_t)ᵀ. Read what the memory currently returns for k, subtract it, write the corrected value with a learned strength β. Erase-then-write instead of pile-on. Plus DPFP, a deterministic feature map that raises the state's usable dimension.
buys: Constant-size state at inference (no growing KV cache), linear time, and a memory that can correct stale bindings
Beats sum-rule linear attention and Performer on WikiText-103 and synthetic retrieval; can carry state across segments
The mechanism inside Gated DeltaNet, Qwen3-Next and Kimi Linear — the 'remember cheaply' thread's answer to recall
costs: Still a compressive fixed-size memory: worse than softmax at exact long-range recall; did not match Transformer-XL at large state sizes

The update is inherently sequential (S_t depends on S_{t−1}): in 2021 it trained with a per-token CUDA kernel — fast at small head dims (63K vs 33K words/s against the PyTorch Transformer) but not tensor-core friendly and unable to scale head dimension — so three years passed before a chunkwise-parallel form (Jun 2024) and a decay gate (Dec 2024) made it competitive at scale
Sensitive to normalisation; not a drop-in for a pretrained softmax model

chatbot2k.why: KV is cheap at 2K; softmax wins on quality per parameter

rag32k.why: as the cheap layers of a hybrid

agent1m.why: in a 3:1 hybrid — never as the only attention type if you need needle recall

pickWhen.verdict: Ignored for three years, then the centre of 2025. Right whenever the memory bill binds and a few exact layers can cover recall.

name: RoPE — Rotary Position Embedding

source.title: RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding
source.authors: Su, Lu, Pan, Murtadha, Wen, Liu (Zhuiyi)
source.evidence: First appeared on Su Jianlin's blog kexue.fm/archives/8265 (23 Mar 2021; GitHub ZhuiyiTechnology/roformer created 2021-03-22; EleutherAI cites the post 'accessed 18-April-2021'). arXiv: [v1] Tue, 20 Apr 2021 09:54:06 UTC

secondary.label: Blog: 'Transformer升级之路：2、博采众长的旋转式位置编码' (kexue.fm/archives/8265)
EleutherAI, 'Rotary Embeddings: A Relative Revolution' (same day as arXiv v1)

problem: Relative position in the score helps (Shaw, T5) but costs an n×n bias tensor or per-layer tables. Wanted: relative-position dependence with the cheapness of absolute encoding — and something that survives *linearised* attention, which biases do not.
idea: Rotate q_m and k_n by angle m·θ_i in each 2-D dimension pair (θ_i geometric, base 10,000 — the sinusoid frequency ladder). Then q_mᵀk_n depends only on m−n. Zero parameters, applied once to Q and K, nothing added to the residual stream.
buys: Relative position for free: no bias tensor, no table, KV-cache friendly, decays with distance
Works with linear attention (the paper's selling point) — which is why every 2025 hybrid can still use it
Became the default: GPT-J → PaLM → LLaMA → everything; and gave the field a *knob* (θ) that made 2023's context extension possible
costs: Does not extrapolate on its own: perplexity blows up past training length — the failure ALiBi attacked and PI/NTK/YaRN patched
Base θ must be chosen for the target length; a 10K-base model needs surgery to reach 128K
Position is baked into cached keys, complicating cache reuse — MLA has to keep a separate 'decoupled RoPE' sub-dimension because of it

rag32k.why: with a large enough θ (or trained at 32K)

coding128k.why: θ = 500K–1M or YaRN; Llama 3.1 / Code Llama style

agent1m.why: RoPE for local layers, NoPE for global (Llama 4 iRoPE), or DroPE-style removal — pure RoPE at 1M is on thin ice

pickWhen.verdict: The most successful positional idea ever, and the reason 2023 was spent stretching it.

name: ALiBi — Attention with Linear Biases

source.title: Train Short, Test Long: Attention with Linear Biases Enables Input Length Extrapolation
source.authors: Press, Smith, Lewis (UW / FAIR / Allen AI)

secondary.label: MPT-7B ('use ALiBi rather than positional embeddings'; StoryWriter 65K)

problem: Sinusoidal, learned and RoPE models all fall apart past their training length. And training long is expensive — can you train at 1,024 and serve at 2,048+ for free?
idea: No positional embeddings at all. Add a fixed, head-specific penalty −m·|i−j| to the pre-softmax scores, with m a geometric sequence per head (not learned). Distance is the only positional signal.
buys: Train at 1,024, extrapolate to 2,048+ with equal-or-better perplexity than a sinusoidal model trained at 2,048; ~11% faster and 11% less memory
Zero parameters, trivial to implement, played well with stability (MosaicML)
Made cheap fine-tune-time context changes possible (MPT-7B-StoryWriter 65K)
costs: The linear penalty is a strong recency prior: it extrapolates in perplexity largely by making attention effectively local — far-away exact retrieval (needle, long copy) is weak
A bias on every score breaks the plain FlashAttention fast path until kernels grew ALiBi support
No relative-position signal usable by linear attention; the LLaMA/GPT-4-era mainstream went RoPE + θ scaling instead

rag32k.why: perplexity holds; retrieval over the whole 32K does not

coding128k.why: cross-file recall needs far tokens; ALiBi discounts them

pickWhen.verdict: It buys length in perplexity and sells long-range recall. Right for train-short-serve-longer small models; wrong for anything retrieval-heavy.

name: Self-attention Does Not Need O(n²) Memory

source.title: Self-attention Does Not Need O(n²) Memory

oneLiner: Chunked attention with a running softmax in JAX — O(√n) memory for exact attention, five months before FlashAttention fused it into a fast kernel.
whyFootnote: Direct precursor to a node already on the timeline (FlashAttention).
